# `nish/net/tls/schedule`

The TLS 1.3 key schedule and transcript hash (RFC 8446 §4.4.1, §7.1, §7.3) for the three cipher suites `nish/net/tls` negotiates.

```ts
import {
  TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,
  TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,
  TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256,
  TLS_IV_SIZE,
  TlsTranscript,
  tlsBinderKey,
  tlsBinderKeyInto,
  tlsBinderVerify,
  tlsDeriveSecret,
  tlsDeriveSecretHeld,
  tlsDeriveSecretInto,
  tlsEarlySecret,
  tlsEmptyHash,
  tlsExpandLabel,
  tlsExtract,
  tlsFinishedVerifyData,
  tlsFinishedVerifyDataHeld,
  tlsFinishedVerifyDataInto,
  tlsHandshakeSalt,
  tlsHandshakeSaltInto,
  tlsHandshakeSecret,
  tlsHandshakeSecretHeld,
  tlsMasterSecret,
  tlsMasterSecretHeld,
  tlsMasterSecretInto,
  tlsPskEarlySecret,
  tlsPskEarlySecretInto,
  tlsResumptionPsk,
  tlsResumptionPskInto,
  tlsSuiteHashLength,
  tlsSuiteKeyLength,
  tlsTrafficIv,
  tlsTrafficKey,
  tlsTrafficKeysFromHeld,
  tlsTrafficKeysInto,
} from "nish/net/tls/schedule";
```

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsTranscript" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlstranscript">

The running transcript hash of RFC 8446 §4.4.1: every handshake message, header included, in the order sent, over the negotiated suite's hash.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

The schedule is a chain of HKDF steps over the suite's hash, SHA-256 for
`TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` and `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` and SHA-384 for
`TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Without a PSK it runs:

```text
early      = HKDF-Extract(0, 0)
handshake  = HKDF-Extract(Derive-Secret(early, "derived", ""), ECDHE)
c/s hs traffic = Derive-Secret(handshake, "c hs traffic" / "s hs traffic", CH..SH)
master     = HKDF-Extract(Derive-Secret(handshake, "derived", ""), 0)
c/s ap traffic, exporter = Derive-Secret(master, "c ap traffic" / "s ap traffic" / "exp master", CH..server Finished)
```

</scalar-callout>

A resumed handshake (RFC 8446 §2.2) starts from the ticket's PSK instead,
and binds the ClientHello to it before anything else is derived:

```text
PSK        = HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption master, "resumption", ticket_nonce, HashLen)
early      = HKDF-Extract(0, PSK)
binder key = Derive-Secret(early, "res binder", "")
binder     = HMAC(Expand-Label(binder key, "finished", "", HashLen), Hash(truncated ClientHello))
handshake  = HKDF-Extract(Derive-Secret(early, "derived", ""), ECDHE)
```

and goes on from the handshake secret as the full handshake does.

Every function takes the hash length (32 or 48) rather than a suite, because
that is all that changes between them; `tlsSuiteHashLength` turns a suite
into one. The traffic key and IV are here too, because T2's record layer
needs them and RFC 8448 prints them beside the secrets.

<scalar-detail title="In place">

Each step also has an `*Into` form that computes in an
`HkdfScratch` the caller owns and writes into the caller's array, and
`TlsTranscript` resets and reads its hash in hashers it allocated once, so
a handshake that keeps its state in a connection slot can run the whole
schedule inside `using a = arena()` blocks and leave the arena where it was
(TLS-3 in `docs/security/tls.md`). The scratch is wiped by every step.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Held">

Each step also has a `*Held` form that reads its secrets from
`Secret`s the caller holds and writes the secret it derives over the bytes
of one, in place, so a connection keeps each stage of the schedule in one
`Secret` for its life and ratchets it: `tlsDeriveSecretHeld`,
`tlsHandshakeSecretHeld`, `tlsMasterSecretHeld`, and the two that answer
plain bytes, `tlsFinishedVerifyDataHeld` (`verify_data` goes on the wire)
and `tlsTrafficKeysFromHeld` (the cipher reads the key and IV). Every
plain intermediate is wiped before it returns.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets are `Secret`s">

The one-shot functions take every secret they
read (a traffic secret, the ECDHE secret, a stage of the schedule) as a
`Secret<u8[]>` (`nish:secret`) and answer every secret they derive as one;
each reads its key only inside `exposeWith` and wipes the intermediates it
made (the "derived" salts, the `finished_key`, the zero inputs) before it
returns, and HMAC wipes its key blocks. The caller owns what it is handed
and wipes it. What a `Secret` cannot reach is TLS-1 in
`docs/security/tls.md`. The transcript hashes, the labels and a Finished
message's `verify_data` are public and stay plain.

</scalar-detail>

Written from RFC 8446, not ported from another implementation.

## tlsBinderKey

The binder key of a resumption PSK: `Derive-Secret(early, "res binder", "")` (RFC 8446 §7.1).

```ts
function tlsBinderKey(
  hashLength: i32,
  earlySecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="earlySecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The early secret from `tlsPskEarlySecret`. It stays the caller's: this does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the binder key, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsBinderKeyInto

`tlsBinderKey` in place: `Derive-Secret(early, "res binder", "")`, written at `out[0]`. The scratch is
wiped before it returns.

```ts
function tlsBinderKeyInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  hashLength: i32,
  earlySecret: u8[],
  out: u8[],
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, which this computes in and wipes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="earlySecret" type="u8[]" required>

The early secret, plain. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

Where the binder key is written, from index 0; the caller owns and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsBinderVerify

Whether `binder[binderOff .. binderOff + binderLength)` is the PSK binder
RFC 8446 §4.2.11.2 asks for: the HMAC, under `finished_key =
Expand-Label(binderKey, "finished", "", HashLen)`, of
`truncatedHash[hashOff .. hashOff + hashLength)`, the transcript hash of
the ClientHello up to its binders list. A binder that is not HashLen bytes
long, or whose window is not inside `binder`, is `false` (row 9 of
"Resumption" in `docs/security/tls.md`). The comparison reads every byte
whatever it finds; the binder the server computed is wiped before it
returns, as `tlsFinishedVerifyDataInto` wipes the finished key and the
scratch.

```ts
function tlsBinderVerify(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  hashLength: i32,
  binderKey: u8[],
  truncatedHash: u8[],
  hashOff: i32,
  binder: u8[],
  binderOff: i32,
  binderLength: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, which this computes in and wipes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="binderKey" type="u8[]" required>

The binder key from `tlsBinderKeyInto`, plain. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="truncatedHash" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the hash of the ClientHello up to its binders list.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashOff" type="i32" required>

Where in `truncatedHash` the `hashLength` bytes of that hash start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="binder" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the binder the client sent, usually the received ClientHello.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="binderOff" type="i32" required>

Where in `binder` the client's binder starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="binderLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the client's binder is.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when the client's binder matches the one the server computed, so the client holds the PSK.

</scalar-field>

## tlsDeriveSecret

Derive-Secret (RFC 8446 §7.1): Expand-Label of `prk` with `label` and a transcript hash, HashLen bytes
held as a `Secret`.

```ts
function tlsDeriveSecret(
  hashLength: i32,
  prk: Secret<u8[]>,
  label: string,
  transcriptHash: u8[],
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are derived.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="prk" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The stage of the schedule to derive from. It stays the caller's: this function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="label" type="string" required>

The label without its `"tls13 "` prefix, such as `"s hs traffic"`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The transcript hash the secret is bound to, all of it used as the context.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the HashLen derived bytes, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsDeriveSecretHeld

`tlsDeriveSecret` into a held `Secret`: Derive-Secret (RFC 8446 §7.1) of
`prk` with `label` and the transcript hash `transcriptHash[hashOff ..
hashOff + hashLength)`, written over the HashLen bytes `dst` holds. `dst`
may be `prk`. Panics unless `hashLength` is 32 or 48 and both hold
HashLen bytes.

```ts
function tlsDeriveSecretHeld(
  hashLength: i32,
  prk: Secret<u8[]>,
  label: string,
  transcriptHash: u8[],
  hashOff: i32,
  dst: Secret<u8[]>,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="prk" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held stage of the schedule to derive from. It is only overwritten when it is also `dst`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="label" type="string" required>

The label without its `"tls13 "` prefix, such as `"c ap traffic"`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the transcript hash, which is public.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashOff" type="i32" required>

Where in `transcriptHash` the `hashLength` bytes of the hash start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dst" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held secret whose bytes the result overwrites. The caller still owns and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsDeriveSecretInto

`tlsDeriveSecret` in place: Derive-Secret (RFC 8446 §7.1) of `prk` with
`label` and the transcript hash `transcriptHash[hashOff .. hashOff +
hashLength)`, its HashLen bytes written at `out[0]`. The scratch is wiped
before it returns. It panics as `hkdfExpandLabelInto` does, a window outside
its array included.

```ts
function tlsDeriveSecretInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  hashLength: i32,
  prk: u8[],
  label: string,
  transcriptHash: u8[],
  hashOff: i32,
  out: u8[],
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, which this computes in and wipes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="prk" type="u8[]" required>

The stage of the schedule to derive from, plain. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="label" type="string" required>

The label without its `"tls13 "` prefix, such as `"s hs traffic"`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the transcript hash.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashOff" type="i32" required>

Where in `transcriptHash` the `hashLength` bytes of the hash start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

Where the derived secret is written, from index 0; the caller owns and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEarlySecret

The early secret with no PSK: HKDF-Extract of HashLen zeros under a zero salt (RFC 8446 §7.1). The zero
salt and the zero input are wiped before it returns.

```ts
function tlsEarlySecret(
  hashLength: i32,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the early secret, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEmptyHash

The hash of the empty string, the transcript `Derive-Secret(., "derived", "")` hashes.

```ts
function tlsEmptyHash(hashLength: i32): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

48 for SHA-384; any other value runs SHA-256.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The digest of no bytes, in a fresh array. It is public, so it is plain.

</scalar-field>

## tlsExpandLabel

HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 §7.1) over the hash `hashLength` names: `length`
bytes from `prk` (RFC 8446's Secret), the label (without its `"tls13 "`
prefix, which is added) and `context`, held as a `Secret`. It panics as
`hkdfExpandLabelSha256Secret` (or its SHA-384 twin) does.

```ts
function tlsExpandLabel(
  hashLength: i32,
  prk: Secret<u8[]>,
  label: string,
  context: u8[],
  length: i32,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

48 for SHA-384; any other value runs SHA-256.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="prk" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The secret to expand. It stays the caller's: this function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="label" type="string" required>

The label without its `"tls13 "` prefix, such as `"key"` or `"c hs traffic"`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="context" type="u8[]" required>

The public context bytes, usually a transcript hash; empty for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes to derive.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the `length` derived bytes, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsExtract

HKDF-Extract (RFC 5869 §2.2) over the hash `hashLength` names, held as a
`Secret`. Both inputs are `Secret`s, since the schedule salts every extract
after the first with a derived secret; an empty salt keys HMAC as HashLen
zeros do.

```ts
function tlsExtract(
  hashLength: i32,
  salt: Secret<u8[]>,
  ikm: Secret<u8[]>,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

48 for SHA-384; any other value runs SHA-256.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="salt" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The HMAC key. It stays the caller's: this function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ikm" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The input keying material. It stays the caller's as well.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the HashLen-byte PRK, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsFinishedVerifyData

A Finished message's `verify_data` (RFC 8446 §4.4.4): the HMAC of the
transcript hash under `finished_key = Expand-Label(baseKey, "finished", "",
HashLen)`, where `baseKey` is the sender's handshake traffic secret. The
`finished_key` is wiped before it returns; `verify_data` goes on the wire,
so it is plain.

```ts
function tlsFinishedVerifyData(
  hashLength: i32,
  baseKey: Secret<u8[]>,
  transcriptHash: u8[],
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="baseKey" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The sender's handshake traffic secret. It stays the caller's: this does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The transcript hash up to, and not including, the Finished message.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The HashLen bytes of `verify_data`, plain, in a fresh array.

</scalar-field>

## tlsFinishedVerifyDataHeld

`tlsFinishedVerifyData` from a held base key and a window of a transcript:
the HMAC of `transcriptHash[hashOff .. hashOff + hashLength)` under
`finished_key = Expand-Label(baseKey, "finished", "", HashLen)` (RFC 8446
§4.4.4). The finished key is held and wiped before it returns;
`verify_data` goes on the wire, so it is plain. Panics unless `hashLength`
is 32 or 48 and `baseKey` holds HashLen bytes.

```ts
function tlsFinishedVerifyDataHeld(
  hashLength: i32,
  baseKey: Secret<u8[]>,
  transcriptHash: u8[],
  hashOff: i32,
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="baseKey" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The sender's held handshake traffic secret. It stays the caller's: this does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the transcript hash up to the Finished message.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashOff" type="i32" required>

Where in `transcriptHash` the `hashLength` bytes of the hash start.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The HashLen bytes of `verify_data`, plain, in a fresh array.

</scalar-field>

## tlsFinishedVerifyDataInto

`tlsFinishedVerifyData` in place: the HMAC of `transcriptHash[hashOff ..
hashOff + hashLength)` under `finished_key = Expand-Label(baseKey,
"finished", "", HashLen)` (RFC 8446 §4.4.4), written at `out[at]`. The
finished key is wiped before it returns, and so is the scratch.

```ts
function tlsFinishedVerifyDataInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  hashLength: i32,
  baseKey: u8[],
  transcriptHash: u8[],
  hashOff: i32,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, which this computes in and wipes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="baseKey" type="u8[]" required>

The sender's handshake traffic secret, plain. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the transcript hash up to the Finished message.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashOff" type="i32" required>

Where in `transcriptHash` the `hashLength` bytes of the hash start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

Where `verify_data` is written. It goes on the wire, so it is plain.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where in `out` the HashLen bytes of `verify_data` start.

</scalar-field>

## tlsHandshakeSalt

The salt the handshake secret is extracted under, `Derive-Secret(early,
"derived", "")` (RFC 8446 §7.1): what `tlsHandshakeSecret` derives and
wipes itself, answered for a caller that extracts in place.

```ts
function tlsHandshakeSalt(
  hashLength: i32,
  earlySecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="earlySecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The early secret. It stays the caller's: this function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the salt, which the caller owns and wipes once the extract is done.

</scalar-field>

## tlsHandshakeSaltInto

`tlsHandshakeSalt` in place: `Derive-Secret(early, "derived", "")`, the
salt a resumed handshake extracts its handshake secret under, written at
`out[0]`. The caller wipes it once the extract is done. The scratch is wiped
before it returns.

```ts
function tlsHandshakeSaltInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  hashLength: i32,
  earlySecret: u8[],
  out: u8[],
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, which this computes in and wipes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="earlySecret" type="u8[]" required>

The early secret, plain. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

Where the salt is written, from index 0.

</scalar-field>

## tlsHandshakeSecret

The handshake secret: HKDF-Extract of the ECDHE secret under
`Derive-Secret(early, "derived", "")`, which is wiped before it returns.

```ts

  hashLength: i32,
  earlySecret: Secret<u8[]>,
  ecdhe: Secret<u8[]>,
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="earlySecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The early secret. It stays the caller's: this function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

The shared secret of the key exchange. It stays the caller's to wipe as well.

A fresh `Secret` holding the handshake secret, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsHandshakeSecretHeld

`tlsHandshakeSecret` into a held `Secret`: HKDF-Extract of `ecdhe` under
`Derive-Secret(early, "derived", "")`, written over `dst`'s HashLen bytes.
The salt is wiped before it returns; `dst` may be `earlySecret`. Panics
unless `hashLength` is 32 or 48 and `earlySecret` and `dst` hold HashLen
bytes.

```ts
function tlsHandshakeSecretHeld(
  hashLength: i32,
  earlySecret: Secret<u8[]>,
  ecdhe: Secret<u8[]>,
  dst: Secret<u8[]>,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="earlySecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held early secret. It is only overwritten when it is also `dst`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ecdhe" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held shared secret of the key exchange. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dst" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held secret whose bytes the handshake secret overwrites. The caller still owns and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsMasterSecret

The master secret: HKDF-Extract of HashLen zeros under
`Derive-Secret(handshake, "derived", "")`, which is wiped before it returns,
as the zeros are.

```ts
  hashLength: i32,
  handshakeSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
```

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="handshakeSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The handshake secret. It stays the caller's: this function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the master secret, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsMasterSecretHeld

`tlsMasterSecret` into a held `Secret`: HKDF-Extract of HashLen zeros under

`handshakeSecret`. Panics unless `hashLength` is 32 or 48 and both hold


The hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="handshakeSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held handshake secret. It is only overwritten when it is also `dst`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dst" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held secret whose bytes the master secret overwrites. The caller still owns and wipes it.

## tlsMasterSecretInto

`tlsMasterSecret` in place: HKDF-Extract of HashLen zeros under

The early secret of a resumed handshake: HKDF-Extract of the PSK under a

A fresh `Secret` holding the early secret, which the caller owns and wipes.

`tlsPskEarlySecret` in place: HKDF-Extract of `psk` under a zero salt

## tlsResumptionPsk

The PSK a ticket stands for: `HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret,
"resumption", ticket_nonce, HashLen)` (RFC 8446 §4.6.1).

```ts

  hashLength: i32,
  resumptionMasterSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
  ticketNonce: u8[],
): Secret<u8[]>
```

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are derived.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="resumptionMasterSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The connection's resumption master secret. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

## tlsResumptionPskInto

`tlsResumptionPsk` in place: `HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret,
"resumption", ticketNonce[nonceOff .. nonceOff + nonceLength), HashLen)`

returns. A nonce window outside `ticketNonce`, or longer than 255 bytes,
panics, as `hkdfExpandLabelInto` does.

```ts
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  hashLength: i32,
```

The hash length, 32 or 48, which is also how many bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

The connection's resumption master secret, plain. It stays the caller's.

</scalar-field>

The array that holds the ticket's `ticket_nonce`, which is public.

</scalar-field>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

Where the PSK is written, from index 0; the caller owns and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsSuiteHashLength

The hash length of `suite`: 32 for the two SHA-256 suites, 48 for
`TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, and 0 for any suite this module does not
negotiate, which is how a caller tells the two apart.

```ts
function tlsSuiteHashLength(suite: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

A cipher suite code point, such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The suite's hash length in bytes (32 or 48), or 0 for a suite this module does not negotiate.

</scalar-field>

## tlsSuiteKeyLength

The AEAD key length of `suite`: 16 for AES-128-GCM, 32 for the other two, 0 for an unknown suite.

```ts
function tlsSuiteKeyLength(suite: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

A cipher suite code point, such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The suite's AEAD key length in bytes (16 or 32), or 0 for a suite this module does not negotiate.

</scalar-field>

## tlsTrafficIv

The 12-byte IV a traffic secret gives `suite`'s record protection (RFC 8446
§7.3), held as a `Secret`; empty for a suite this module does not negotiate.

```ts

  suite: i32,
  trafficSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
```

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The negotiated cipher suite, such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The traffic secret the IV comes from. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the 12-byte IV, or an empty one for an unknown suite. The caller owns
    and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsTrafficKey

The AEAD key a traffic secret gives `suite`'s record protection (RFC 8446
§7.3), held as a `Secret`; empty for a suite this module does not negotiate.

```ts
function tlsTrafficKey(
  suite: i32,
  trafficSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The negotiated cipher suite, such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The traffic secret the key comes from. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the suite's key (16 or 32 bytes), or an empty one for an unknown suite.
    The caller owns and wipes it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsTrafficKeysFromHeld

`tlsTrafficKeysInto` from a held traffic secret: the AEAD key it gives
`suite` (RFC 8446 §7.3) written into `key`, which must be the suite's key
length, and its 12-byte IV into `iv`. Both stay plain, since the cipher
reads them. `false`, writing nothing, for a suite this module does not
negotiate, a secret that is not its hash's length, or a key or IV array of
the wrong length.

```ts
function tlsTrafficKeysFromHeld(
  suite: i32,
  trafficSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
  key: u8[],
  iv: u8[],
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The negotiated cipher suite, such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The held traffic secret, of the suite's hash length. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="key" type="u8[]" required>

Where the AEAD key is written: an array of exactly the suite's key length (16 or 32 bytes).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="iv" type="u8[]" required>

Where the IV is written: an array of exactly 12 bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when the key and IV were written; `false`, with nothing written, for a bad suite or length.

</scalar-field>

## tlsTrafficKeysInto

`tlsTrafficKey` and `tlsTrafficIv` in place: the AEAD key a traffic secret
gives `suite` (RFC 8446 §7.3) written into `key`, which must be the suite's
key length, and its 12-byte IV into `iv`. `false`, writing nothing, for a
suite this module does not negotiate, a secret that is not its hash's
length, or a key or IV array of the wrong length. When it derives, the
scratch is wiped before it returns.

```ts
function tlsTrafficKeysInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  suite: i32,
  trafficSecret: u8[],
  key: u8[],
  iv: u8[],
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, which this computes in and wipes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The negotiated cipher suite, such as `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="u8[]" required>

The traffic secret, plain, of the suite's hash length. It stays the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="key" type="u8[]" required>

Where the AEAD key is written: an array of exactly the suite's key length (16 or 32 bytes).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="iv" type="u8[]" required>

Where the IV is written: an array of exactly 12 bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when the key and IV were written; `false`, with nothing written, for a bad suite or length.

</scalar-field>

## TlsTranscript

The running transcript hash of RFC 8446 §4.4.1: every handshake message,
header included, in the order sent, over the negotiated suite's hash.

`hash` reads the hash so far from a copy, so the transcript keeps going: the
schedule takes it after ServerHello, after Certificate, after
CertificateVerify and after the server's Finished. `restartWithMessageHash`
is the HelloRetryRequest rule: the first ClientHello is replaced by the
synthetic `message_hash` message holding its hash.

Both hashers are kept so that the field types do not depend on the suite;
only the one `hashLength` names is fed. So are a fresh pair, which `reset`
starts the transcript again from, and a twin pair `hashInto` reads the hash
through: all six are made once, so a transcript reused for the next
connection with `reset` allocates nothing that outlives a call.

```ts
class TlsTranscript
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsTranscript(hashLength: i32)` | Makes an empty transcript and all six of its hashers, once, so that `reset` can reuse them. |
| `hash(): u8[]` | The transcript hash of everything absorbed so far, in a fresh array; the transcript goes on. |
| `restartWithMessageHash(): void` | Replaces the transcript so far, which must be exactly the first ClientHello, by `message_hash` (type 254, a 24-bit length of HashLen, then Hash(ClientHello1)), as RFC 8446 §4.4.1 has a server do before it absorbs its HelloRetryRequest. |
| `update(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): void` | Absorbs `data[off .. off + len)`, a whole handshake message or part of one. |
